overview.title: Measures Of Inflation
overview.definition: Measures of inflation are quantitative indices used to track the average change in prices of a basket of goods and services over time in an economy, serving as critical gauges of purchasing power and macroeconomic stability.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Frequently tested in UPSC Prelims regarding CPI vs. WPI, base years, institutional mandates (RBI Monetary Policy Committee), and in Mains GS-3 under 'Inclusive Growth and Mobilization of Resources'.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Measures Of Inflation.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of National Income and Macroeconomics

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Consumer Price Index (CPI)**: Measures price changes from the perspective of the retail consumer, tracking out-of-pocket expenditures on a fixed basket of goods and services.
• **Wholesale Price Index (WPI)**: Measures the price of a basket of wholesale goods prior to the retail stage, focusing heavily on raw materials and intermediate goods.
• **Implicit Price Deflator (GDP Deflator)**: Measures the ratio of nominal GDP to real GDP, covering all domestically produced goods and services without a fixed basket.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Headline Inflation (includes all commodities including volatile food and fuel) vs. Core Inflation (excludes volatile food and energy items to gauge underlying demand pressures).

items.definition: Headline inflation captures total inflation including volatile items like food and fuel, while Core inflation strips out food and energy to reveal long-term structural inflation trends.
Statutory body under the RBI Act, 1934 tasked with maintaining CPI inflation at 4% with a band of +/- 2%.
Proposed alternative to WPI that measures price changes from the perspective of domestic producers, excluding taxes and trade margins.
Landmark committee that recommended shifting India's primary inflation anchor from WPI to CPI-Combined.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Rural vs. Urban CPI Divergence**: Disaggregated indices capture varying consumption baskets; rural baskets are heavily weighted towards food, while urban baskets feature higher weights for housing and services.
• **Regional Supply Bottlenecks**: Logistics corridors and regional agricultural production zones heavily influence localized CPI-Food fluctuations across different states.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Frequent revisions in base years, volatile food supply chains, and statistical gaps in tracking unorganized retail prices.
• **Policy Interventions**: Strengthening buffer stocks (PM-GKAY), digitizing supply chains, and transitioning towards a comprehensive Producer Price Index (PPI).

items.title: Mnemonic for Inflation Targeting Range
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'Four plus-minus two'.
• **Decoded Meaning**: Target is 4% CPI inflation with an upper tolerance of 6% (4+2) and lower tolerance of 2% (4-2).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly verifies numeric statements regarding the RBI mandate.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: 'W is for Wholesale, C is for Consumer, G is for Gross'. Remember that WPI excludes services, CPI includes retail services, and GDP Deflator includes everything produced.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that WPI includes services. This is incorrect—WPI tracks goods only (Primary Articles, Fuel & Power, Manufactured Products), whereas CPI tracks both goods and services.

Mains Value Addition: Emphasize the shift from WPI to CPI as a paradigm shift in monetary governance, ensuring that monetary policy directly protects the purchasing power of common citizens rather than wholesale producers.

keyTakeaways: CPI-Combined is India's official benchmark for headline inflation targeting managed by the RBI's MPC.
WPI tracks wholesale goods prices and excludes services, making it less representative of household cost of living.
GDP Deflator offers the broadest coverage of domestic economic inflation as its basket changes dynamically with production.
